content.short: ENS maps human-readable names to machine-readable addresses and identifiers on the Ethereum blockchain.
content.description: The Ethereum Name Service (ENS) is a distributed, open, and extensible naming system built on the Ethereum blockchain. Its core function is to translate human-friendly names into machine-readable identifiers, enabling straightforward interactions across the Ethereum ecosystem. Names like 'alice.eth' can resolve to Ethereum addresses or other cryptocurrency addresses, content hashes that reference off-chain data, and associated metadata. By providing a decentralized directory for names, ENS simplifies wallet addresses, contract interactions, and onboarding while remaining compatible with standard Ethereum tooling.
content.meta: ENS provides decentralised naming for wallets and websites. Discover ENS and other Web3 Wallet Tools on Lancers Web3 Explorer.

resources.title: How ENS Normalization Works
resources.tldr: Two names can look identical to a person and be entirely different strings to a machine, which is precisely how spoofing works. Explains the normalization step that closes that gap.

resources.title: How ENS Names Evolved
resources.tldr: From a flat ownership model for .eth names through subnames and permissions to ENSv2's registry-native design. Good for understanding why the architecture ended up shaped this way.

resources.title: What Makes ENS a Protocol
resources.tldr: The argument that ENS is naming infrastructure and not a product: stable resolution rules, open standards, and many independent interfaces all reading the same records.
